newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally to close on bottom-fishers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally to close on bottom-fishers.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered from early lows and rallied to close sharply higher on Friday as local and foreign bargain hunters stepped in.

"The market heated up at midsession after being dead in the morning. They woke up at last to the fact that fundamentally sound stocks had been hit too hard and went on a bargain-hunting spree. Construction stocks in particular moved ahead," said a trader from the Inverlat brokerage.
The blue chip IPC index closed up 54.43 points, or 1.65 percent, at 3,347.66. Volume was not spectacular at 79.9 million shares traded, but much livlier than early trade.
On the broad market scoreboard, a total of 103 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 70 to 18.

Financial stock GFInver headed the gainers and analysts noted this stock had been volatile ever since the takeover of its banking arm by Banco Santander was recently announced, on speculation over the issue price of new shares to help finance the deal.
Construction firms Tribasa and Bufete featured among the gainers. Traders noted the 1997 budget contained details of infrastructure spending that would favor this sector.
Financial stock BBV-Probursa headed the losers at heavy volume, but traders noted this was inflated by cross trades. Traders said that losers mostly fell "on normal trading adjustments."
Technical analysts noted the IPC broke resistance at 3,300 points, and that the following target was at 3,450 points, although adjustments due to consolidation could not be ruled out on the way.
"The bourse is tracing an inverted head-and-shoulders formation which points towards all-time highs," said Leonor Gonzalez, technical analyst at the BBV-Probursa brokerage.
